fix_commit.message: Bug 2018075 - Add missing write barrier in BaseScript::swapData r=jandem
fix_commit.author: Jon Coppeard

findings.title: Missing write barrier on PrivateScriptData buffer-allocator pointer in BaseScript::swapData
findings.message: BaseScript::swapData() updates the BaseScript::data_ pointer (a BufferAllocator-managed allocation holding PrivateScriptData) using only `data_.set(zone(), other)`. That GCStructPtr::set() call only triggers a write barrier for the *contents* pointed to by data_ (i.e. the GC things referenced from inside PrivateScriptData), but it performs no write/read barrier for the buffer allocation pointer itself. Before Bug 2002790, PrivateScriptData was a plain malloc'd UniquePtr-owned buffer with no GC-tracing concerns of its own, so this was fine. After Bug 2002790 migrated PrivateScriptData to be allocated via the nursery-aware BufferAllocator (gc::NewSizedBuffer), the data_ pointer itself became a GC-managed edge that can point into the nursery and needs to be traced/barriered like any other GC edge (via TraceBufferEdge), not just the GC things nested within it. Because swapData() replaces data_ without first tracing/barriering the old buffer pointer, an incremental or generational GC can lose track of the old nursery-allocated buffer when a script is delazified/relazified (e.g. swapData is invoked from createPrivateScriptData/fullyInitFromStencil/relazify). This leads to a stale/dangling buffer pointer later being traced as if it were a valid BufferAllocator allocation, producing a SEGV / `isAllocated(alloc)` assertion failure in BufferAllocatorInternals.h when the tracer (js::PrivateScriptData::trace -> TraceManuallyBarrieredGCCellPtr -> BufferAllocator::isNurseryOwned/traceEdge) accesses the corrupted/freed allocation -- effectively a use-after-free of the buffer allocation metadata.
findings.suggestion: Before overwriting data_ with the new buffer in swapData (and before clearing it in releaseData/freeData), explicitly trace/barrier the old buffer allocation pointer itself (not just its GC-thing contents) using TraceBufferEdge when the zone needs a marking barrier, mirroring the fix: check `if (data_ && zone()->needsMarkingBarrier())` and call `TraceBufferEdge(zone()->barrierTracer(), this, &data_, "BaseScript::swapData barrier")` prior to `data_.set(zone(), other)`. More generally, provide a GCStructPtr/edge abstraction that barriers both the buffer-allocation pointer and its contents uniformly so future buffer-allocator migrations don't reintroduce this class of bug.

ground_truth.root_cause: BaseScript::swapData/releaseData assumed that GCStructPtr::set() barriers were sufficient for updating the data_ pointer, which was true when PrivateScriptData was a plain heap allocation. Once Bug 2002790 made data_ a BufferAllocator-managed (nursery-capable) allocation, the pointer itself became a GC edge requiring its own trace/write barrier (via TraceBufferEdge), which was not added at the same time, leaving a gap between allocation-strategy change and barrier coverage.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Missing write barrier on PrivateScriptData buffer-allocator pointer in BaseScript::swapData
